audit_status.source_base: Greek 1 Corinthians text tradition, draft aligned to public-domain comparison layer later
audit_status.review_note: Compact complete draft reviewed for sexual immorality case, communal arrogance, discipline for restoration, Passover/leaven imagery, judging inside/outside.

verses.restored: It is actually reported that there is sexual immorality among you, and such sexual immorality as is not even among the nations: someone has his father's wife.

familiar.text: It is reported commonly that there is fornication among you, and such fornication as is not so much as named among the Gentiles, that one should have his father’s wife.

modern.text: It is actually reported that there is sexual immorality among you, and of a kind that is intolerable even among pagans: A man has his father’s wife.

original.text: Ὅλως ἀκούεται ἐν ὑμῖν πορνεία, καὶ τοιαύτη πορνεία ἥτις οὐδὲ ἐν τοῖς ⸀ἔθνεσιν, ὥστε γυναῖκά τινα τοῦ πατρὸς ἔχειν.

verses.restored: And you are puffed up, and have you not rather mourned, so that the one who did this work might be removed from your midst?

familiar.text: And ye are puffed up, and have not rather mourned, that he that hath done this deed might be taken away from among you.

modern.text: And you are proud! Shouldn’t you rather have been stricken with grief and have removed from your fellowship the man who did this?

original.text: καὶ ὑμεῖς πεφυσιωμένοι ἐστέ, καὶ οὐχὶ μᾶλλον ἐπενθήσατε, ἵνα ⸀ἀρθῇ ἐκ μέσου ὑμῶν ὁ τὸ ἔργον τοῦτο ⸀ποιήσας;

verses.restored: For I indeed, absent in body but present in spirit, have already judged as present the one who worked this out,

familiar.text: For I verily, as absent in body, but present in spirit, have judged already, as though I were present, concerning him that hath so done this deed,

modern.text: Although I am absent from you in body, I am present with you in spirit, and I have already pronounced judgment on the one who did this, just as if I were present.

original.text: Ἐγὼ μὲν γάρ, ⸀ἀπὼν τῷ σώματι παρὼν δὲ τῷ πνεύματι, ἤδη κέκρικα ὡς παρὼν τὸν οὕτως τοῦτο κατεργασάμενον

verses.restored: in the name of our Lord Jesus, when you are gathered together and my spirit with the power of our Lord Jesus,

familiar.text: In the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, when ye are gathered together, and my spirit, with the power of our Lord Jesus Christ,

modern.text: When you are assembled in the name of our Lord Jesus and I am with you in spirit, along with the power of the Lord Jesus,

original.text: ἐν τῷ ὀνόματι τοῦ κυρίου ἡμῶν ⸀Ἰησοῦ, συναχθέντων ὑμῶν καὶ τοῦ ἐμοῦ πνεύματος σὺν τῇ δυνάμει τοῦ κυρίου ἡμῶν ⸁Ἰησοῦ,

verses.restored: to hand such a one over to the adversarial one for destruction of the flesh-pattern, so that the spirit may be saved/healed in the day of the Lord.

familiar.text: To deliver such an one unto Satan for the destruction of the flesh, that the spirit may be saved in the day of the Lord Jesus.

modern.text: hand this man over to Satan for the destruction of the flesh, so that his spirit may be saved on the Day of the Lord.

original.text: παραδοῦναι τὸν τοιοῦτον τῷ Σατανᾷ εἰς ὄλεθρον τῆς σαρκός, ἵνα τὸ πνεῦμα σωθῇ ἐν τῇ ἡμέρᾳ τοῦ ⸀κυρίου.

verses.restored: Your boasting is not beautiful/good. Do you not know that a little leaven leavens the whole lump?

familiar.text: Your glorying is not good. Know ye not that a little leaven leaveneth the whole lump?

modern.text: Your boasting is not good. Do you not know that a little leaven works through the whole batch of dough?

original.text: Οὐ καλὸν τὸ καύχημα ὑμῶν. οὐκ οἴδατε ὅτι μικρὰ ζύμη ὅλον τὸ φύραμα ζυμοῖ;

verses.restored: Clear out the old leaven, so that you may be a new lump, just as you are unleavened; for Messiah, our Passover, has been sacrificed.

familiar.text: Purge out therefore the old leaven, that ye may be a new lump, as ye are unleavened. For even Christ our passover is sacrificed for us:

modern.text: Get rid of the old leaven, that you may be a new unleavened batch, as you really are. For Christ, our Passover lamb, has been sacrificed.

original.text: ἐκκαθάρατε τὴν παλαιὰν ζύμην, ἵνα ἦτε νέον φύραμα, καθώς ἐστε ἄζυμοι. καὶ γὰρ τὸ πάσχα ⸀ἡμῶν ἐτύθη Χριστός·

verses.restored: Therefore let us keep the feast, not with old leaven, nor with leaven of harm and wickedness, but with unleavened sincerity and truth.

familiar.text: Therefore let us keep the feast, not with old leaven, neither with the leaven of malice and wickedness; but with the unleavened bread of sincerity and truth.

modern.text: Therefore let us keep the feast, not with the old bread, leavened with malice and wickedness, but with the unleavened bread of sincerity and of truth. Expel the Immoral Brother

original.text: ὥστε ἑορτάζωμεν, μὴ ἐν ζύμῃ παλαιᾷ μηδὲ ἐν ζύμῃ κακίας καὶ πονηρίας, ἀλλʼ ἐν ἀζύμοις εἰλικρινείας καὶ ἀληθείας.

verses.restored: I wrote to you in the letter not to mix together with sexually immoral people,

familiar.text: I wrote unto you in an epistle not to company with fornicators:

modern.text: I wrote you in my letter not to associate with sexually immoral people.

original.text: Ἔγραψα ὑμῖν ἐν τῇ ἐπιστολῇ μὴ συναναμίγνυσθαι πόρνοις,

verses.restored: not at all meaning the sexually immoral of this world, or the greedy and swindlers, or idolaters, since then you would need to go out of the world.

familiar.text: Yet not altogether with the fornicators of this world, or with the covetous, or extortioners, or with idolaters; for then must ye needs go out of the world.

modern.text: I was not including the sexually immoral of this world, or the greedy and swindlers, or idolaters. In that case you would have to leave this world.

original.text: ⸀οὐ πάντως τοῖς πόρνοις τοῦ κόσμου τούτου ἢ τοῖς πλεονέκταις ⸀καὶ ἅρπαξιν ἢ εἰδωλολάτραις, ἐπεὶ ⸀ὠφείλετε ἄρα ἐκ τοῦ κόσμου ἐξελθεῖν.

verses.restored: But now I wrote to you not to mix together if anyone named sibling is sexually immoral, greedy, idolater, slanderer, drunkard, or swindler; with such a one, not even to eat.

familiar.text: But now I have written unto you not to keep company, if any man that is called a brother be a fornicator, or covetous, or an idolater, or a railer, or a drunkard, or an extortioner; with such an one no not to eat.

modern.text: But now I am writing you not to associate with anyone who claims to be a brother but is sexually immoral or greedy, an idolater or a verbal abuser, a drunkard or a swindler. With such a man do not even eat.

original.text: νῦν δὲ ἔγραψα ὑμῖν μὴ συναναμίγνυσθαι ἐάν τις ἀδελφὸς ὀνομαζόμενος ᾖ πόρνος ἢ πλεονέκτης ἢ εἰδωλολάτρης ἢ λοίδορος ἢ μέθυσος ἢ ἅρπαξ, τῷ τοιούτῳ μηδὲ συνεσθίειν.

verses.restored: For what is it to me to judge those outside? Do you not judge those inside?

familiar.text: For what have I to do to judge them also that are without? do not ye judge them that are within?

modern.text: What business of mine is it to judge those outside the church? Are you not to judge those inside?

original.text: τί γάρ ⸀μοι τοὺς ἔξω κρίνειν; οὐχὶ τοὺς ἔσω ὑμεῖς κρίνετε,

verses.restored: But the Divine judges those outside. Remove the harmful one from among yourselves.

familiar.text: But them that are without God judgeth. Therefore put away from among yourselves that wicked person.

modern.text: God will judge those outside. “Expel the wicked man from among you.”

original.text: τοὺς δὲ ἔξω ὁ θεὸς ⸀κρίνει; ⸀ἐξάρατε τὸν πονηρὸν ἐξ ὑμῶν αὐτῶν.

translation_notes: The discipline language is aimed at communal protection and ultimate restoration, not humiliation or permanent exile.
Flesh in verse 5 is rendered flesh-pattern to avoid implying body-hatred; the issue is destructive embodied pattern and community corruption.
